title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 11 Areas Related to Circles (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
short_title: Class 10 Maths · Ch 11 Areas Related to Circles
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number. Use the value of π given in the question. No calculator.

patterns.T1: Sector area (incl. equal sectors, find the angle)
patterns.T2: Arc length / perimeter of a sector

S1.name: Sector and segment: minor, major, quadrant
S1.tip: Sector = two radii + arc; segment = chord + arc. Major angle = 360° − θ. 'Sector' alone means the minor one.

S2.name: Area of a sector
S2.tip: Area of a sector = θ/360 × πr².

S3.name: Equal sectors and the angle
S3.tip: n equal sectors: angle 360°/n, area πr²/n.

S5.name: Perimeter of a sector
S5.tip: Perimeter of a sector = arc + 2r. Don't forget the two radii.

S6.name: Area = ½ × arc × r (reverse questions)
S6.tip: Area = ½ × arc × r. Use it to find r or θ backwards.

S7.name: Clock hands, wipers, swept areas
S7.tip: Minute hand 6° per minute; hour hand 30° per hour; wipers and umbrella ribs are equal sectors.

S8.name: Area of a segment (60°, 90°, 120°)
S8.tip: Segment = sector − triangle. 90°: ½r²; 60° and 120°: (√3/4)r² for the triangle.

S9.name: Shaded regions and case studies
S9.tip: Shaded regions: add and subtract known shapes; use the π the question gives.

questions.explanation: Both true and R is the reason (NCERT note in 11.1).
questions.assertion: Area of the major segment = πr² − area of the minor segment.
questions.reason: The minor and major segments formed by a chord together make up the whole circle.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
